solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Husband presented with new Omega out of repect

definitions.note: the clue's misspelling of respect, a sense of honour or tribute

indicators.note: something new is made over, so these letters take a fresh order

explanation.surface: A husband given a new Omega watch, purely as a gesture of respect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' is a link meaning 'arising from'; the printed 'repect' is a typo for 'respect'.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying tribute to someone is showing them honour, the respect a vassal once owed his lord.

clue.text: Two intruments producing music for dance

parts.note: together with the next word this asks for two instruments; the first is a horn
the clue's spelling of instruments; the second instrument is a pipe

explanation.surface: A pair of instruments playing dance music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two intruments' (printed without its S) asks for two instrument names placed side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively sailors' dance, and the tune played for it, is music for dancing.

clue.text: A disfigurement hidden by the old lady's cosmetic

indicators.note: hidden by means enclosed within, so one part sits inside the other

parts.note: the old lady is slang for mother, MA; the 's joins her to the cosmetic
a scar is a disfiguring mark

explanation.surface: An elderly woman covering a blemish with her make-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the old lady' is a British slang term for one's mother; 'hidden by' reads as concealment by make-up but is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Make-up for darkening eyelashes is a cosmetic product.

clue.text: Size may be right when altered

indicators.note: altered means changed, so the letters are put in a different order

explanation.surface: A tailor's thought: the size might fit once the garment is altered.
explanation.definitionFit: The measurement around something's middle is its size or bulk.

clue.text: Group of characters in The Rover heading off on a venture?

indicators.note: the head, or first letter, of the name is taken away

parts.note: Sir Ralph the Rover is the pirate villain of Southey's poem The Inchcape Rock
a bet is a venture, a risky stake

explanation.surface: Someone reading about a character in a book called The Rover who sets off on an adventure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' looks like setting out, but it removes the R from RALPH, leaving ALPH.
explanation.definitionFit: The letters of a writing system form a set of characters, from A to Z.

clue.text: Suitably wearing much less, so don't interfere

indicators.note: wearing means having on, so one part is put around the other

parts.note: let alone means much less, as in he can't walk, let alone run
well means suitably, properly

explanation.surface: Advice to someone dressed scantily: better not to meddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing much less' suggests skimpy clothes; 'much less' is LET ALONE, which wears WELL.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom tells someone to leave things as they are, not meddling.

clue.text: Workers not working with complete ease

parts.note: hands are workers, as in farmhands
down means out of action, as a computer system can be

explanation.surface: Staff who are idle and completely at ease.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means winning easily, with no effort at all.

clue.text: Battery found by artist aboard canal boat

indicators.note: aboard means on the boat, so one part goes inside the other

parts.note: a barge is a flat-bottomed canal boat
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: An artist on a narrowboat finds a battery.
explanation.definitionFit: A sustained bombardment of artillery is a battery, as in a battery of guns.

clue.text: Hearing test in building at the end

parts.note: to try is to test

indicators.note: at the end picks the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A hearing test held in a building at the far end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearing test' reads as one medical check; 'Hearing' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Judging a case in court is giving it a hearing.

clue.text: Repair centre

definitions.meaning: to repair somewhere is to go there
a holiday centre or seaside destination

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: going to a place, and a place people go to for holidays.

clue.text: Ratings cooked unknown fish

indicators.note: cooked means falsified or tampered with, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: Y is an algebraic unknown, like x and z

explanation.surface: Sailors preparing a meal of some unidentified fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ratings' looks like sailors, but its letters are rearranged to STINGRA.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat ray with a venomous tail spine is a kind of fish.

clue.text: Lots go here after prices tumble?

definitions.text: Lots go here after prices tumble?

parts.words: Lots go here after prices tumble?
parts.note: lots are items for sale at auction; in this kind of sale the asking price starts high and falls until someone bids

explanation.definitionFit: A sale where the price is lowered step by step until a buyer accepts fits lots going after prices fall.

clue.text: What little girls may do in their home theatre?

definitions.text: What little girls may do in their home
definitions.meaning: children pretend to keep a household as a game
a building where plays are put on

explanation.definitionFit: Playing at keeping a home is a children's game, and a building for drama is a theatre.

clue.text: Spot wartime leader dropping piece of litter

indicators.note: dropping means letting fall, so a letter is removed

parts.note: Stalin led the Soviet Union in the Second World War

indicators.note: a piece here is just its first letter

explanation.surface: Catching sight of a wartime leader who drops a scrap of rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping' looks like littering, but it removes the L (the first of 'litter') from the leader's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A mark or blemish on fabric is a spot.

clue.text: Real card tricks expected from me?

parts.note: practical means real or actual, as opposed to theoretical
the joker is a card in the pack

explanation.surface: Someone doing real card tricks, as might be expected of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'card tricks' reads as a conjuror's act; split it, so 'card' is the joker and 'tricks expected from me?' is the definition, spoken by the prankster.
explanation.definitionFit: A prankster who plays tricks on people is the one who would say tricks are expected from him.

clue.text: Juicy Argentine fruit

indicators.note: juicy suggests something squeezed or mashed, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A succulent piece of produce from Argentina.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Juicy' looks like a description of the fruit but signals rearranging 'Argentine'.
explanation.definitionFit: A small loose-skinned orange citrus is a fruit.

clue.text: Overwhelm in a Parisian court

parts.note: un is French for a
to court someone is to date them

explanation.surface: Being overwhelmed in a Paris courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' reads as a lawcourt but is the verb to woo.
explanation.definitionFit: To flood something is to overwhelm it.

clue.text: Flee: go with dog as well direct

parts.note: a go is a turn, someone's chance to play
to dog is to tail or follow closely
and means as well, in addition
to direct a business is to run it

explanation.surface: Fleeing instructions: go off with a dog, and be sure to do it properly.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn around and escape from danger is to flee, an idiom for retreating.

clue.text: Lots consumed by plump teenagers

indicators.note: consumed by means swallowed up inside, so the letters sit within these words

explanation.surface: Large quantities of food eaten by overweight teenagers.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal word for a great many, an indefinitely large number.

clue.text: Genuine trouble, reportedly, getting beer

parts.note: real means genuine

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: Real trouble comes from drinking beer, so they say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' turns AIL into ALE by sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Cask-conditioned ale, as championed by British drinkers' campaigns, is a kind of beer.

clue.text: False report an eccentric put about

indicators.note: put about means placed around, so one part wraps the other

parts.note: a card is an eccentric or comic person

explanation.surface: An odd person spreading a rumour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put about' reads as spreading a story, a natural partner for 'False report', but here it means placed around.
explanation.definitionFit: A canard is an unfounded rumour, a false story.

clue.text: Large specimen, not small

indicators.note: not means without, so the following letter is removed

parts.note: a sample is a specimen taken for testing
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothes labels

explanation.surface: A large specimen, not a small one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not small' reads as part of the description; it removes an S.
explanation.definitionFit: Ample means generous in size, plentiful or large.

clue.text: Force prisoners to exercise

parts.note: cons are convicts, prisoners
to train is to exercise, as athletes do

explanation.surface: Making inmates take exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: To compel or restrict someone is to force them, a close synonym.

clue.text: Journey on foot, then miles in carriage

indicators.note: in places one letter within the other word

parts.note: a trap is a light horse-drawn carriage

explanation.surface: Walking, then covering miles by carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A long walk or trek is a journey made on foot.

clue.text: Drink provided by Italian after a commercial traveller returned

indicators.note: after says the Italian comes behind the earlier letters
returned means sent back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative, a commercial traveller
IT is short for Italian, as in gin and it (Italian vermouth)
if means provided that

explanation.surface: A salesman back from his travels has a drink, supplied by an Italian host.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns REP into PER; 'by' just places IT beside IF.
explanation.definitionFit: A drink taken before a meal to whet the appetite is an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Fruit and nuts, mostly

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: bananas is slang for mad, nuts

explanation.surface: A dish of fruit and nuts, by and large.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' looks like a food alongside fruit, but it is slang for crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: A long yellow tropical fruit, sold in bunches.

clue.text: Waste long periods of time in prisons

parts.note: dung is animal waste
eons are immeasurably long ages

explanation.surface: Wasting years of one's life behind bars.
explanation.definitionFit: Underground cells in a castle are prisons, often dark and grim.

clue.text: A bit each

parts.note: a piece is a bit or portion

explanation.definitionFit: Apiece is an adverb meaning for each one, as in a pound each.
